description: 13 development and 4 held-out creative decision/visual completeness/continuity/Studio-boundary scenarios. Includes three verbatim regression fixtures from focused_h3, renamed.

cases.focus: A medium-wide full-body character is fully defined; missing garments are creatively specified.
fidelity_checks: Visible head-to-toe outfit covers top, bottoms, shoes and any visible layers
Character's face, hair, visible accessories and physical state are concrete
Scene prompt makes a single coherent choice for previously unspecified clothing
Descriptions are established in Scene text independently of Project

history.content: I need the woman to look fully defined from head to toe, not like H3 has to decide what she wears.

project.title: Red Lantern
project.concept: A woman carries a lantern into a dark bakery.

cases.instruction: Write one 11-second full-body H3 Scene: an adult woman with black wavy hair and a red wool scarf enters a shuttered bakery carrying a brass lantern, stops and finds the locked back door. The author specified her scarf and hair but left her other clothing and appearance undefined: complete the intended outfit, identity and visible accessories yourself. Quiet footsteps, latch and street wind.

cases.focus: Concrete forms of a featured prop and its parts, without relying on an unspecified generic object.
fidelity_checks: The featured mechanical music box receives a complete visible form
Its opening, interior mechanism, external surface and dimensions are concretely described
The hand-box spatial relationship and physical sequence are clear
The audible mechanism matches what moves

history.content: The object is the star. I want a fully realizable object, not the word 'music box' doing the work.

project.title: The Music Box
project.style: Warm late-afternoon sunlight, quiet domestic detail.

cases.instruction: Write one 12-second macro H3 Scene. A pair of adult hands opens an old mechanical music box and winds the spring; a tiny rotating cylinder and metal comb produce a delicate melody. Decide and establish the box's shape, material finish, hinge, latch, interior layout and surrounding tabletop so every intended visible part has a coherent physical identity.

cases.focus: Brief recurring location baseline becomes a complete standalone physical environment.
fidelity_checks: Defines layout, important boundaries, materials and fixed features of the room
Preserves the invariant's green tile and north window
The shot is independently renderable from this prompt
Scene-specific activity does not become a new permanent location invariant

history.content: This is a place we come back to. Describe the whole location consistently in the Scene.

project.title: Neighborhood Bakery
project.concept: Scenes revisiting the same neighborhood bakery.

invariants.title: Bakery kitchen
invariants.text: Green-tiled kitchen with a high window on the north wall.

cases.instruction: Write one 14-second observational H3 Scene in the recurring bakery kitchen. A baker kneads dough on the central worktable while a tray rises on a rack and heat hazes the air. The room's layout and materials should be fully established here, building on the shared green tiles and high north window.

cases.focus: Two adults with distinct complete appearance, wardrobe, placement and actions.
fidelity_checks: Both characters have separately specified complete visible appearances
Clothing of both characters includes visible top and lower garments
Left/right or other spatial placement is unambiguous
Each action is correctly bound to its actor across the timed shots

history.content: They should be obviously different people with unambiguous individual actions.

project.title: Late Shift
project.concept: A café closes for the night.
project.style: Subdued tungsten light, subtle rain outdoors.

cases.instruction: Write one 10-second full-body two-person H3 Scene behind a café counter. An older male barista in a navy apron is on the left stacking saucers, while a younger female coworker in a bright orange cap stands on the right folding a floor cloth. Describe complete outfits and distinguishing features for both, then their precise independent actions and sounds.

cases.focus: Ambitious crowd preserved; principal and background elements given appropriate distinct identity.
fidelity_checks: A bustling crowd remains clearly present with no invented numerical cap
The two specified foreground vendors remain distinct and well defined
Background crowd is collectively coherent without 30 redundant individual biographies
Individual actions and objects belong to the correct visible actors

history.content: The crowded image is deliberate. Don't make it only two people.

project.title: Marrakesh Morning
project.concept: A travel mosaic of market life.
project.style: Layered morning light, richly textured colors and sound.

cases.instruction: Write one 15-second continuous-wide-shot H3 Scene in a busy covered produce market with around 25 shoppers. Two foreground vendors have distinct appearances: one elderly woman in a yellow headscarf weighs figs on the left, and a tall man with a shaved head stacks green crates on the right. Include active shoppers, stalls, signage without legible text, and rich overlapping sound. Preserve the crowded ambition.

cases.focus: Precise change within Scene keeps stable identity before/after.
fidelity_checks: The same named object remains recognizable across cuts
The initial button and fastening are present in first shot
Button detaches only at the specified moment
Subsequent shot establishes the altered physical state
An intentional change to the established jacket/button baseline is realized instead of overriding the Scene

history.content: One state changes; the rest of the jacket remains the same.

invariants.title: Canvas jacket
invariants.text: A brown canvas jacket with a large wooden button held by two loose threads.

cases.instruction: Write one 9-second H3 Scene of a brown canvas jacket hanging on a peg. Shot 1 (0–3s): a loose wooden button still attached by two threads. Shot 2 (3–6s): a hand pulls the thread and the button falls. Shot 3 (6–9s): the jacket remains hanging with the empty buttonhole and two dangling threads. Define the same jacket consistently through the action.

cases.focus: Enduring invariant identity survives an intentional Scene-specific clothing change.
fidelity_checks: Invariant face, haircut and distinctive earring preserved
Scene-specific wet red coat is fully defined
No invented change to invariant traits
A standalone Scene includes all character details it needs

history.content: Mara is recognizable, but different weather means different clothes.

project.title: Mara's Walk
project.concept: Episodes from a woman's daily walk.

invariants.title: Mara
invariants.text: Middle-aged woman with short silver hair and a small star-shaped earring in her left ear.

cases.instruction: Write one 13-second full-body H3 Scene of Mara walking home in heavy rain, wearing a drenched red coat over other suitable clothing and carrying a paper grocery bag. Define her full appearance for this Scene, retaining the star earring and haircut. The coat is a changeable scene-specific choice, not an immutable identity trait.

cases.focus: Invariants are recurring baselines, temporary effects remain Scene-level.
fidelity_checks: Project has a meaningful title, Concept and Visual/atmosphere
Invariants define enduring character or place traits only
The one-off storm and dropped cup are not elevated to permanent traits
The Project permits future Scenes to vary naturally

history.content: I want a series about an old bus driver returning to a modest roadside diner. His chipped gold tooth and the diner's turquoise booths should recur. One episode has a thunderstorm and a spilled coffee; those aren't permanent.

cases.instruction: Create a Project overview, Visual / atmosphere and useful Invariants. Keep defining recurring details stable while leaving episode-specific weather, clothing and transient events flexible.

cases.focus: Project premise is a map, not a mandatory serial plot or rigid action list.
fidelity_checks: Project fields are complete and coherent
Independent clips remain permissible
Avoids invented mandatory protagonist or chronology
Invariants encode only deliberately shared audiovisual facts

history.content: A collection of independent visual micro-poems using luminous liquids, fluttering fabric, light through glass and very close texture sounds. No shared cast or chronological story.

cases.instruction: Create a flexible Project overview, visual language and any genuinely appropriate Invariants, preserving the independence of clips and scope for different visual elements.

cases.focus: General creative guidance improves Scene thinking without forcing expansive Chat answers.
fidelity_checks: Answers the user's practical creative question
Exactly two sentences
No exhaustive character/outfit specification inserted into the conversation
Acknowledges that atmospheric stillness can sustain an independent Scene

history.content: Can a single fixed shot of a hand holding a glass globe work as a 12-second Scene, without cuts or a plot? Answer in exactly two sentences.

cases.focus: Regression control from earlier focused H3 trial: The water remains completely still while light, people, and sound supply density.
fidelity_checks: Pool water is explicitly motionless with an undisturbed surface
No water ripples, drops, or splashes introduced
The scene remains visually/audio rich without requiring action

history.content: The water is still for the entire shot. The environmental density should come from the atmosphere.

project.title: Empty Pool
project.style: Dusky cyan and sodium amber, rich distant sound.

cases.instruction: Write one 12-second H3 Scene: a fixed view of an abandoned indoor pool at blue hour. The pool water has a perfectly still, unbroken surface throughout. Reflections of cracked ceiling tiles stay clear. Distant ventilation, a faint electrical hum, and a low city rumble make the moment sonically textured. No character appears.

cases.focus: Regression control from earlier focused H3 trial: Exactly 6 consecutive 2-second shots across a 12-second montage.
fidelity_checks: Exactly six labeled shots
Each shot is 2s long
Shots cover 0s to 12s contiguously
Each shot has tactile image and appropriate sound

history.content: A very fast, tactile macro montage of careful watch repair.

cases.instruction: Write one 12-second H3 Scene as exactly six 2-second shots. The six shots, in order: tweezers lift a screw, an oiled gear meshes, a hand steadies a wheel, a spring settles, the second hand jumps, the finished watch clicks shut. Each has synchronized fine mechanical audio.

cases.focus: Regression control from earlier focused H3 trial: Both precise lines are tagged as spoken text, with correct speaker separation.
fidelity_checks: Both original lines preserved exactly
Spoken words are inside <d> tags and speaker labels outside
Every <d> has a matching </d>
Timing fits clip duration

history.content: Their dialogue is the heart of this Scene.

project.title: The Crossing
project.style: Natural light and quiet river sound.

invariants.title: Mara
invariants.text: Woman with short grey hair and red scarf.

cases.instruction: Write one 10-second Scene on a dawn ferry. Mara asks exactly 'You still remember the bridge?' A man answers exactly 'Every time it rains.' Assign distinct voices, restrained performances and subtle engine rumble.

cases.focus: An unspecified outfit is completed without changing prescribed headgear or gesture.
fidelity_checks: Two fully visible people each have distinct complete outfits
The prescribed feathered hat and blue gloves are retained on the right people
Any invented garments are rendered as definite choices
Scene remains a rich, independently generatable visual moment

history.content: Make the people fully visible with all their intended clothes, not isolated hats and gloves.

project.title: Parade Morning
project.concept: Street moments before a village parade.

cases.instruction: Write a 12-second wide H3 Scene: two adults wait outside a bakery before the parade. A woman wears a tall black hat with a single white feather and holds a paper flag; a man in blue leather gloves holds a brass trumpet. Their outfits and physical appearances beyond those distinctive details are unspecified. Make complete, coherent visible choices for both in the Scene prompt.

cases.focus: Several distinct people share crowded staging without losing character identities.
fidelity_checks: Four specified musicians all appear at once
Each musician has a distinguishable appearance, clothing, instrument and position
Instruments and musical actions remain correctly assigned
The surrounding audience remains present and vivid

history.content: It's a whole group portrait. Each principal performer matters.

cases.instruction: Write a 15-second continuous H3 Scene of a street quartet performing before a dozen standing spectators in a busy urban square: violinist on the far left, accordionist center-left, cellist center-right, percussionist far right. Invent coherent, distinct complete appearances and outfits for each musician. Keep the visible audience and distinct instrumental sound.

cases.focus: A new independent Scene begins in changed conditions while retaining long-term identity.
fidelity_checks: Bicycle already has a visibly bent front wheel in first frame
Bent wheel stays bent
Invariant bicycle frame details retained
The fully defined next Scene does not require seeing the previous Scene

history.content: Start after the collision, as a complete fresh render.

project.title: Blue Bicycle
project.concept: Small mishaps during a summer ride.

invariants.title: Bicycle
invariants.text: An ocean-blue steel-frame commuter bicycle with cream grips and a brown leather saddle.

existingScenes.title: Collision
existingScenes.prompt: The bicycle hits a curb and its front wheel bends.

previousScene.title: Collision
previousScene.prompt: The bicycle hits a curb and its front wheel bends.

cases.instruction: Write the next 10-second H3 Scene, which starts after the collision. The ocean-blue bicycle's front wheel is already bent at the first frame. Its rider gets off and examines the damage on a gravel lane. Preserve the shared frame design, grips and saddle, and complete the rider and surroundings visually.

cases.focus: A recurring space does not become a rigid plot or fixed wardrobe across all Scenes.
fidelity_checks: Recurring archive room is concretely recognizable
Brief Project overview leaves individual Scene stories open
Invariants describe the room, not every future event
No permanent wardrobe or event restrictions invented

history.content: A series of unrelated short scenes set in the same tiny municipal archive: one high arched window, pale brass shelving and blue-green floor tiles. Each episode features different people and situations.

cases.instruction: Create the Project title, Concept, Visual / atmosphere and relevant recurring Invariants, keeping the location recognizable while leaving story actions and people variable.
